purpose: Freeze the strongest defensible Catalyst N1 K26-class hardware/RTL comparison boundary before vendor implementation results are observed.

reproduction_environment.vivado_version_role: Project reproduction choice. The pinned Catalyst K26 Tcl does not require a version; the same Catalyst commit explicitly uses Vivado 2025.2 for AWS F2 and this thesis already standardizes on Vivado/Vitis 2025.2.

catalyst_k26.readme_flow_caveat: The pinned README omits -tclargs synth_only. In the pinned build_kria.tcl, default mode=full creates and closes the project without launching synthesis. M13.5 therefore invokes the source's documented synth_only mode before run_impl.tcl and records this as tooling normalization, not a Catalyst RTL modification.

physical_programming_boundary.reason: The pinned fpga/kria directory provides no board XDC, no Vivado block design/processing-system integration, and no write_bitstream step. The supplied wrapper exposes AXI ports as top-level ports. The source-supported flow therefore establishes synthesis/routed implementation characterization, not a directly programmable KV260 image.
physical_programming_boundary.rule: Do not claim physical Catalyst KV260 execution unless a separate, explicitly documented board integration is constructed and validated. Absence of that integration is a platform/tooling boundary, not a behavioral disagreement.

project_m12_physical.scope: Validation-capable M12.5 image including computational core, workload image, VIO/debug shell, physical trace path, and passive timing counter.

fairness_rules: M13.5 is a reproducibility and architecture audit, not a performance contest.
Always disclose that Catalyst's pinned K26 Tcl targets xczu5ev-sfvc784-2-i while the project's accepted M12 image targets xck26-sfvc784-2LV-c; do not silently treat the part strings as identical.
Report Catalyst resource usage together with the Available counts emitted by the same Vivado report. Compare raw counts and fractions only with the target-part distinction visible.

Disclose capacity and feature scope: Catalyst wrapper is 2 cores x 256 neurons with pool depth 4096/core and broader NoC/management/learning-related RTL; the thesis M12.5 image is a smaller serialized validation core with VIO/trace/debug instrumentation.
Do not infer architectural efficiency from raw LUT/BRAM/DSP totals when feature sets and capacities differ.

Do not compare M12 latency/throughput against Catalyst unless an equivalent architectural-timestep workload and on-fabric cycle boundary are measured for Catalyst. K26 implementation reports alone do not provide that evidence.
Do not compare power values: M12 intentionally excluded power/energy from its validated claim set and Catalyst's report_power estimate would not share the same measurement methodology.
A failed physical-programming attempt caused by missing board integration is Class H/tooling-platform evidence, not a neuron-model discrepancy.

automated_preflight: exact Catalyst source pin and K26 blobs verified
Kria wrapper elaborates from the pinned RTL under Icarus >=12
M13.5 manifest/parser tests and complete project regression pass
vendor_reproduction: Vivado 2025.2 synth_only flow completes on pinned Catalyst source without tracked-source edits
run_impl.tcl completes route_design at the upstream target part and 10 ns clock
synthesis and routed utilization/timing reports are preserved
routed WNS/WHS and major resources are parsed into a machine-readable result
pass_boundary.strongest_boundary_rule: If the vendor routed flow succeeds but the pinned release still lacks a directly programmable KV260 integration, M13.5 may close at routed implementation as the strongest source-supported hardware boundary, provided the physical limitation is explicitly documented.
